transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-02 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonah Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (HaloEdge Head of ML), Ethan Bowers (HaloEdge Platform Eng), Lena Ortiz (HaloEdge Security), Marco (Data Scientist, sometimes labelled Speaker 4)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Goal: scope a pilot to validate throughput/latency and establish success criteria for production rollout. Focus on QPS, concurrency, input/output token distribution, benchmark plan and timeline.
- Preliminary constraints: mix of short chat completions (~8-40 tokens response) and longer contextual summarizations (200-800 output tokens), spikey bursts during business hours. Security: on-prem PII concerns, SSO/SAML and KMS needed.

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do quick intros then jump into the pilot goals, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE, and with me is Jonah our systems engineer.
00:08 Jonah: hi all, happy to be here, i'll try and be technical, apologies if i miss a name once in a while.
00:12 Priya: thanks, i'm priya, head of ml at haloedge, we've got ethan on infra, lena on security and marco on modelling.
00:18 Ethan: yeah thanks, quick note -- we're on a 3rd party vpc with cloud provider and also running some on-prem edge boxes for low latency in europe.
00:27 Maya: great, scope for today is to agree success criteria, collect workload signals (qps, concurrency, token mix), and outline a bench plan + timeline.
00:34 Priya: perfect, high level -- our product is a conversational assistant plus a long-form summarization service. The assistant is chatty, avg user turns 5, but responses short, like 10-30 tokens. Summarizer receives a doc and returns 300-700 tokens depending on doc. We expect heavy burstiness at 11-1 pm PT and again 2-3 am GMT, also weekend dips.
01:02 Jonah: ok that helps. do you have current telemetry e.g. p50/p95 latency, qps per endpoint, and token distribution?
01:08 Priya: we have some logs but need to sanitize, we'll try export a 2-week window. i can say approximate numbers: baseline assistant 7 qps sustained across region, peaks up to 180 qps for a 10min window; summarizer baseline 0.6 qps, peaks to 12 qps. concurrency for assistant often spikes to 120 concurrent requests during peak minute windows.
01:33 Maya: good, so pilot goals: 1) demonstrate we can hit p95 latency SLA of 300ms for assistant in hosted mode at target peak qps and concurrency; 2) for summarizer, p95 of 2.5s at expected concurrency; 3) validate cost per 1k tokens under the projected config; 4) verify security posture for shared traces. does that align?
01:59 Priya: yes, mostly. for the assistant we actually want an internal SLA of p95 200ms, externally 300ms. can you get p95 200ms at 180 qps peak?
02:11 Jonah: we'll design a bench to test that; likely need to push to dedicated pools or tuned batching. i want to call out kv cache behavior -- if the assistant uses conversation state heavily we can reuse kv cache and reduce token compute, but if it's stateless then latency increases.
02:29 Marco (labelled Speaker 4): sorry, i didn't quite catch kv cache -- you mean the k-v lookup inside the transformer? sometimes models need full context append which makes cache less effective.
02:37 Jonah: yeah exactly, i mean the key-value cache at generation time; if you send incremental tokens we can do prefix caching which saves cycles. but depends on how you manage the conversation and model variant.
02:47 Ethan: quick infra Q -- can we run the pilot in our private VPC with a redwood private control plane? we have compliance needs and some datasets are air-gapped.
02:55 Maya: yes we offer private with customer-managed networking; for the pilot we can do either hosted with egress constraints or a private demo in your VPC. for benchmarking we often start in hosted to iterate faster then move workload replay to private to validate network hops.
03:10 Lena: security is key. We need SSO with SAML, role-based access, KMS integration, and audit logs. Also data retention must be configurable to zero or 30 days.
03:22 Maya: understood, we will share SOC2 artifacts and our security checklist. we'll need a short questionnaire answer from you as well.
03:28 Priya: regarding token mix, assistant inputs are usually short (20-60 input tokens), outputs 10-30, but when users paste context it can go up to 1k input tokens for summarizer flows. We also see multi-turn convos where cumulative context grows.
03:45 Jonah: good, for bench plan we'll define three traffic profiles: bursty-chat (assistant), long-form summarization (summarizer), and mixed blended traffic. For each profile we need: sustained qps target, 1-min peak qps, concurrency distribution, and a token-length histogram.
03:59 Marco: we can provide histograms but the exporter may mislabel some tokens because of our tokeniser differences, i can include tokeniser mapping.
04:08 Maya: perfect. timeline idea: week 1 (2026-03-08) we collect traces and baseline metrics; week 2 (2026-03-15) redwood runs initial hosted benches and shares results; week 3 (2026-03-22) we replay workload in private with tuning; week 4 (2026-03-29) joint review and SOW draft. is that realistic?
04:26 Ethan: that sounds aggressive but doable if we prioritize traces early. we need to ensure bench harness runs from our CI so we can reproduce.
04:35 Jonah: our bench harness will accept a request trace (json lines) with timestamps and payloads; we can syntheticize token lengths if needed. one question: what are your success criteria beyond latency? error rate, throughput stability, cost per 1k tokens?
04:49 Priya: success = p95 below thresholds (200ms internal for assistant, 2.5s for summarizer), error rate < 0.5% (client-visible errors), CPU/GPU saturation under 85% during peaks, and cost projection within our budget envelope (we'll share target $/1000 tokens).
05:05 Maya: we will include those as gating criteria in the pilot. for cost projections we need to know model variant (quantized vs fp16) and batching configs. do you have a preferred model family?
05:15 Priya: currently experimenting with open-variant models similar to gpt-medium-sized family, and we prefer int8 for cost but want to check quality regressions.
05:23 Jonah: ok, we'll test fp16 and int8 quantized variants and include qual checks. we'll run A/B on a small eval set you provide to measure generation quality vs baseline.
05:34 Marco: about benchmarks -- how do you handle tail latency noise and network jitter? our global users can hit nodes in eu and na leading to cross-region latencies.
05:44 Jonah: we'll run region-isolated benches to measure pure inference latency and then run end-to-end tests from your VPC to capture network tail. also include jitter injection in the harness to simulate packet loss.
05:57 Lena: also need encryption at rest for KV cache dumps and separate keys per environment.
06:03 Maya: noted, we support customer-managed KMS and can rotate keys. we'll add that to the security deliverables.
06:10 Ethan: curious on autoscaling strategy -- if we hit sudden 10x spikes, will the platform queue or reject? understand you have burst capacity.
06:19 Jonah: good question. policy options: immediate rejection (429), graceful queueing up to short windows, or fallback to a cheaper model variant. for pilot we can enable short queueing and model fallback for non-critical routes.
06:33 Priya: we want graceful degradation, but not for billing-sensitive flows. need a route-level policy.
06:40 Maya: route-level policies supported, we'll include suggested defaults in SOW.
06:44 Marco: one more on telemetry -- can you emit per-token breakdowns and cost attribution per route?
06:50 Jonah: yes, console has token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms and traces. we can include token-attribution exports to your reporting stack. small caveat: attribution for cached prefixes looks like fewer input tokens which may skew unit cost, we'll annotate that.
07:06 Priya: ok, quick headcount: success stakeholders are priya (ml), ethan (platform), lena (security), finance will look at cost. we want a pilot sign-off criteria document before week 4.
07:18 Maya: agreed, we'll produce a sign-off checklist (latency numbers, error rate, cost targets, security artifacts).
07:23 Ethan: anything else on data residency? some EU data must stay in eu region.
07:28 Maya: we can pin region routing and ensure EU inference stays on eu-located instances.
07:32 Priya: final ask: can you provide an estimated cost delta between hosted vs dedicated for our peak profile? even rough numbers would help.
07:39 Jonah: yes, we'll run a sizing calc after we get token histograms; early estimate in the pricing workbook. dedicated usually improves unit cost by 20-40% depending on utilization.
07:50 Marco: small note: our current tokeniser counts differ from standard tiktoken, so when you run benchmarks please use our mapper to reflect real token lengths.
07:58 Maya: we'll accept your mapper and integrate into bench harness.
08:01 Priya: great, then to recap next steps?
08:04 Maya: recap: 1) haloedge provides sanitized 2-week traces + tokeniser mapping (priyaa/marco) by 2026-03-09; 2) redwood sends benchmark template + SOW draft + security artifacts by 2026-03-05; 3) jonah to draft benchmark plan by 2026-03-04; 4) schedule latency deep dive with infra week of 2026-03-15.
08:28 Priya: agreed.
08:30 Lena: one small question on legal - we need a DP addendum for PII handling, can you share sample DPA?
08:36 Maya: yes we'll attach our standard DPA and can tailor it; legal may take 1-2 weeks.
08:42 Ethan: okay thanks, we'll get traces and try to unblock you.
08:46 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in writing.

(End of recording)
